sections.label: FF&E Sourcing and Coordination
sections.h2: Your Furniture Plan Shapes Every Cover You Seat
body: We're your restaurant furniture supplier and FF&E coordinator, from the first look at the floor plan to the last chair on the floor. We plan the seating mix with you, source every piece, and keep samples, orders, freight, and install timing on one schedule, so you can spend opening week training your team and tasting your menu.

You can use our network of hospitality furniture suppliers, or we can coordinate the vendors you already trust. Either way, we work with your designer, architect, and builders, and you approve every selection before an order goes in. We do the work. You guide the process.

sections.label: Floor Plan and Seating Mix
sections.h2: Table Configuration Built for Covers and Turns
body: Every floor plan is a set of trade-offs. Booths are comfortable, and guests settle in. Two-tops that push together let the host seat a party of six without holding a whole section. Bar seats catch walk-ins and solo diners.
We work from your floor plan to find the mix that fits your concept and your volume, with aisles wide enough for servers carrying full trays and a clear path from expo to every table.

The mix also sets your pace. Flexible two-tops and four-tops help a high-volume room keep turning, and booths and lounge seating suit a longer, slower dinner. We match the mix to the night you want to run and the covers you need.

sections.label: Furniture Meets Software
sections.h2: Your Floor Plan, Live on the Host Stand
body: When we also build your restaurant software, the furniture plan carries straight into the host stand. Table numbers, sizes, and combinations from the floor plan become the live floor map your hosts seat from.
So when two four-tops by the window push together for a party of eight, the host stand already knows. Server sections come from the same plan, which keeps the floor and the screen in sync.

faq.q: How much does restaurant furniture cost through Monarch?
faq.a: Every project is scoped to your restaurant, so we don't publish prices. Your written plan includes a budget by category, like seating, tables, booths, patio, and custom pieces, and you approve it before anything is ordered.

faq.q: How long does it take to get restaurant furniture?
faq.a: Lead times vary by piece, maker, and finish, and custom pieces take longer than in-stock seating. We build the schedule backward from your opening date and order the long-lead pieces first, so furniture lands when the space is ready for it.

faq.q: Can you work with our designer and the vendors we already use?
faq.a: Yes. We work alongside your designer, architect, and builders. You can source through our vendor network, or we can coordinate the vendors you already have, with one point of contact for samples, orders, freight, and install timing.

faq.q: What do you need from us to get started?
faq.a: A floor plan or drawings, your design direction or your designer's spec, a target seat count, your opening date, and a budget range. For a remodel, photos of the current room help. We'll walk the space with you, on site or virtual.

faq.q: Do you furnish single restaurants and multi-location groups?
faq.a: Both. For a group, we keep one furniture spec with the same finishes and fabrics across locations, so a new unit matches the rest and a damaged chair can be replaced to match.

faq.q: Do you handle delivery and installation?
faq.a: We coordinate freight, receiving, and install timing with your builders and installers. Deliveries get checked at receiving, so damaged or wrong pieces get caught before they reach the dining room.
